The petitioners are various printing presses and associations in Patna, Bihar. They challenge the process adopted by the respondents, including the Union of India and the State of Bihar, for procuring educational material through a centralized process and short-listing the lowest tenderer. The petitioners argue that this process is arbitrary and irrational, and that it affects public interest.

This case involves the procurement of educational materials through a tender process initiated by the Department of Education, Government of Bihar, for the implementation of the Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FL&N) scheme. The Court previously issued directions in CWJC No.7124 of 2020 regarding the provision of nutritious food and digitizing education processes during the pandemic.

The Ministry of Education (Department of School Education & Literacy) Government of India launched the Integrated Scheme for School Education- Samagra Shiksha in 2018 by subsuming the erstwhile Centrally Sponsored Schemes of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA); Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA); and Teacher Education (TE). The Scheme treats school education as a continuum with the Sustainable Development Goal for Education (SDG-4). The Scheme provides support for the implementation of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 (RTE Act) and is also aligned with the recommendations of National Education Policy, 2020 (NEP). The object is to ensure that all children have access to quality education with an equitable and inclusive classroom environment, taking care of their diverse background, multilingual needs, different academic abilities and making them active participants in the learning process. The RTE Act mandates the appropriate Government to provide free and compulsory elementary education to every child of the age 6 to 14 years in a neighbourhood school. Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha, financial assistance is provided as per the fund sharing pattern as decided by the Ministry of Finance. The Scheme is implemented as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme through a single State Implementation Society (SIS) at the State level. The annual plans are prepared by the States and UTs based on their requirements and priority as reflected in their Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWP &B) Proposals. These plans are then appraised and approved/estimated by the Project Approval Board (PAB) in the Department of School Education & Literacy, Government of India in consultation with the States and UTs as per the programmatic and financial norms of the Scheme, and physical and economic progress of the State for approved interventions. The details of funds released under Samagra Shiksha to the State of Bihar during the last three years, as of 17.2.2022, are provided.

This mission has been launched under the aegis of the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha, which focuses on providing access and retaining children in foundational years of schooling; teacher capacity building; development of high quality and diversified Student and Teacher Resources/Learning Materials; and tracking the progress of each child in achieving learning outcomes. The petition filed on 13 January 2022 challenged the terms upon which Request For Proposal (RFP)/Tender was issued. With the selection of the successful bidder, Telecommunication Consultants India Limited, the challenge expanded to four vital issues: the condition of the tender being tailor-made to oust the petitioners from the process of bidding, favoring the shortlisted tenderer, the process of short-listing of the tenderer(s) and selecting the successful tenderer being vitiated on account of ineligibility, malice and favoritism, and whether the Authority exceeded its jurisdiction in undertaking the process of tender.

The first meeting of the State Steering Committee held on 16 September 2021, headed by Additional Chief Secretary, Education Department, Government of Bihar, took certain decisions for implementing FL&N Mission, and minutes was circulated vide communication dated 06 October 2021. The State Project Director, BEPC, with whom the Central Government was interacting, took over the reins and convened meetings for effective implementation of FL&N Mission. Meetings were held on 04 October 2021, 09 November 2021, and 16 November 2021, where several issues were deliberated upon, and consensus arrived on the basic structure for making available the course material for implementing the FL&N mission.

Petitioner No.1 (Bihar Offset Printers Association) communicated on 03 January 2022 to the Bihar State Textbook Publishing Corporation Ltd. (BSTPC) to intervene, ensuring the tendered work is split into two components. The State Project Director, BEPC, was requested to reconsider the decision. Petitioner no.3 (Patna Offset Press) and Petitioner No.4 (New Ratan Priya) also communicated with the State Project Director, BEPC, seeking changes in the tender terms. The pre-bid meeting on 06 January 2022 involved 20 bidders, including petitioners, and resulted in a Corrigendum dated 11 January, 2022.

The Technical Evaluation Committee reviewed the FL&N Sample Evaluation Committee report and the documents submitted by the parties. In evaluating the technical bid, all the three bidders were declared to be duly qualified, competent, and fully compliant. Concerning one item, i.e. bidder's quality certification: ISO Mark, the committee, while awarding 10 out of 20 marks each to two out of three bidders, left the final decision to be taken by the Purchase Committee. The respondents argue that the procurement of educational materials, such as textbooks, falls under the Bihar Finance (Amendment) Rules, 2005. The Scheme provides support for the implementation of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 (RTE Act) and is also aligned with the recommendations of National Education Policy, 2020 (NEP). The object is to ensure that all children have access to quality education with an equitable and inclusive classroom environment, taking care of their diverse background, multilingual needs, different academic abilities and making them active participants in the learning process. The RTE Act mandates the appropriate Government to provide free and compulsory elementary education to every child of the age 6 to 14 years in a neighbourhood school. Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha, financial assistance is provided as per the fund sharing pattern as decided by the Ministry of Finance. The Scheme is implemented as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme through a single State Implementation Society (SIS) at the State level. The annual plans are prepared by the States and UTs based on their requirements and priority as reflected in their Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWP &B) Proposals. These plans are then appraised and approved/estimated by the Project Approval Board (PAB) in the Department of School Education & Literacy, Government of India in consultation with the States and UTs as per the programmatic and financial norms of the Scheme, and physical and economic progress of the State for approved interventions.
